query: What kinds of expenses tend to get declined, and does it differ by department?

per_column.name: is_declined
per_column.rationale: Directly encodes the decline outcome from the existing 'state' column; this is the core dependent variable the query asks about. Grounded and central to the analysis.

per_column.name: amount_bucket
per_column.rationale: Bins the original 'amount' into low/medium/high, giving a clean axis to see whether declines vary by expense size. Directly derivable from amount; useful for grouping.

per_column.name: dept_decline_rate
per_column.rationale: Per-department decline rate directly targets the 'does it differ by department' part of the query. Computed from department + state, fully grounded. Slightly redundant as an aggregate on each row but analytically valuable.

per_column.name: category_decline_rate
per_column.rationale: Per-category decline rate addresses the 'what kinds of expenses get declined' part directly. Derivable from category + state.

per_column.name: dept_category_decline_rate
per_column.rationale: Interaction of department and category decline rates is exactly the cross-tab the query implies. Grounded and adds a genuine modeling axis beyond the two marginal rates.

per_column.name: high_decline_risk
per_column.rationale: A binary risk flag whose distribution (45/455) nearly mirrors is_declined (46/454), making it largely a restatement/threshold of the already-present decline signals. Derivable from the rate columns but adds little independent leverage.

judge.rationale: The added columns strongly serve the query: is_declined provides the outcome, amount_bucket and the three decline-rate columns give department, category, and their interaction axes for exactly the 'what kinds / by department' comparison requested. All values are soundly derivable from existing fields (state, amount, department, category). Only high_decline_risk is weak, functioning as a near-duplicate threshold of the decline signal rather than a new axis. No hallucinations observed in the evidence samples.
